item.title: Indiana court rejects woman's claim to land after neighbours shift boundary fence
item.description: A legal tussle erupted over a narrow patch of grass between two Indiana neighbors, culminating in a ruling by the Indiana Court of Appeals. They upheld a previous decision in favor of the Goldfarbs, the neighboring property owners. Deanne Ellen Gloppen, attempting to claim ownership via adverse possession, fell short of proving her tax payments included the contested area.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lily Snyder's Haircut Backlash: Reps say she chose buzz cut willingly; she plans to explore donation options
item.description: Clavicular's girlfriend, Lily Snyder, has defended her decision to shave her head despite facing online backlash. The influencer suggested the makeover could help address his acne concerns linked to hair products. However, his representatives insist Snyder made the choice willingly and has no regrets. She had also considered donating her long hair, although her bleached locks may not qualify. Snyder reportedly plans to explore other donation options.

item.title: Brandi Carlile's charity surpasses $10m in grants, earning 2026 award recognition for its impact
item.description: At the 2026 Anthem Awards, Brandi Carlile shines as the Entertainer of the Year, celebrating a remarkable achievement for her Looking Out Foundation, which recently surpassed $10 million in grants to diverse charitable organizations. With a focus on uplifting LGBTQIA2S+ communities, the foundation inspires fans to donate small amounts, emphasizing that even an average contribution of $25 can create significant change.

item.title: Oprah joins Australian charity drive, packing care bag as campaign targets 150,000 donations
item.description: Oprah Winfrey is lending her support to Share the Dignity’s charity initiative by assembling care bags for women in need. This campaign, which runs from November 6 to November 22, 2026, across Australia, aims to gather 150,000 bags filled with essential items and uplifting notes. These care bags will benefit women struggling with homelessness or domestic violence. Donations are accepted at various Bunnings stores or online throughout the campaign duration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK man wins Argos laptop refund battle after court rules activating Windows 11 does not cancel rights
item.description: A landmark court decision has established that buyers can return items purchased online within 14 days of receiving them. A University of Leicester professor successfully challenged retail titan Argos over the return of a laptop. The Court of Appeal ruled that activating pre-installed software does not forfeit the right to a refund. This ruling enhances consumer protection for electronics in the UK, prompting retailers to rethink their return policies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists spent 10 days searching Fiji's seas for a bird believed to number fewer than 50 worldwide but saw none; instead, they uncovered the only known recording of its call, deepening the mystery of its survival.
item.description: An expedition around Gau Island aimed at finding the critically endangered Fiji petrel did not result in any sightings. However, researchers gathered crucial information regarding its call from conversations with local residents. This engagement underlined the vital role that community involvement plays in forest conservation and controlling invasive species, suggesting that collective efforts are key to safeguarding the potential nesting sites of this rare bird.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Madagascar has taken a step towards funding the protection of 4 million hectares of forests across 13 regions, nearly 55% of its forest cover, under a carbon-credit programme targeting 6 million tonnes of annual emissions reductions.
item.description: Madagascar has launched the Ala Velona initiative to safeguard its precious forests and tackle climate change. This ambitious project aims to conserve 4 million hectares of woodland while also generating valuable carbon credits. By showcasing the critical need to protect the island's rich biodiversity and ecosystems, the initiative reinforces the link between environmental stewardship and community livelihoods, highlighting a broader trend toward sustainable resource practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: US stalker ordered to pay $18.6 million after stealing woman's Verizon records with fake warrant
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a federal judge in North Carolina has ordered convicted stalker Robert Michael Glauner to pay $18.632 million to a victim for the emotional trauma inflicted upon her. This judgment, which includes punitive damages, stems from Glauner's harassment after he unlawfully procured her private information with a forged search warrant. He was apprehended while attempting to confront her and remains incarcerated.

item.title: 14-year-old Kansas boy rebuilds lawn care business after strangers raise $36,000 following theft
item.description: Sonny Gallardo, a resourceful 14-year-old from Prairie Village, Kansas, founded a thriving lawn care business over time. However, he faced a major setback when equipment valued at around $20,000 was stolen. In a heartwarming response, his community rallied together, raising over $36,000 via a GoFundMe campaign to help him recover.

item.title: Seacrest Stadium: Board approves $2.7 million project; games expected in August 2027
item.description: Ryan Seacrest is set to make a significant impact in Dunwoody, Georgia, with his contribution to a new football stadium for Dunwoody High School. This ambitious project has secured over $2.7 million in funding and has received the green light to proceed. Construction will commence shortly, aimed at completing the stadium in time for the 2027 football season, providing a hub for community sports and activities.

item.title: Tour Raises $8.5 Million: The Weeknd’s run sets male solo-artist revenue record; $3 million raised in 2026
item.description: The Weeknd's After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour achieved unprecedented success, wrapping up in 2026 with an impressive $8.5 million raised for charitable causes. Spanning 67 cities across five continents, the tour drew over nine million fans, setting the record for the highest-grossing concert tour by a male artist, overtaking Elton John's previous milestone.
